claims.title: Exact event-halfspace and active-set vertex description of finite TV balls
claims.scope: one finite exact rational nominal prior and one rational total-variation radius, below declared state and active-basis caps
assumptions: finite total variation equals the maximum absolute probability difference over events
one event from each nontrivial complement pair is retained with both signs
the final simplex coordinate is eliminated and every active rational basis is exhausted
nonclaims: the exponential event and basis enumeration is not a high-dimensional scalability claim
a TV polytope is a declared ambiguity set rather than an empirical confidence region by itself

claims.title: Exact finite-game reduction of shared-randomness coding over a continuous TV ball
claims.scope: one finite confusion graph, all bounded complete deterministic zero-error prefix codebooks, and one finite rational TV-ball source-law ambiguity set
assumptions: encoder and every decoder share a source-independent codebook seed
the source law is selected independently of the realized seed
a linear payoff over the TV polytope reaches its maximum at a vertex
nonclaims: private encoder randomness is not substituted for shared codebook knowledge
the game minimizes expected prefix length rather than peak length, queueing delay, or decoding error

claims.title: Exact continuous mass-transport replay of a mixed codebook solution
claims.scope: a rational shared codebook mixture whose payoff depends on its mixed expected state-length vector
assumptions: the mixed state-length vector is the convex combination of deterministic state-length vectors
the finite-game adversary rows are every TV-ball vertex
the independent TV transport solver is exact for a fixed rational value vector
nonclaims: agreement between two exact finite constructions does not justify a different ambiguity model
the mixed expected state-length vector does not price the entropy of the shared seed

claims.title: Least-favorable prior identity over a continuous TV ball
claims.scope: the complete bounded deterministic zero-error prefix-code universe, shared codebook randomness, and one rational TV-ball ambiguity set
assumptions: the dual vertex mixture forms a prior barycenter inside the convex TV polytope
the deterministic code universe is complete under the declared caps
the exact finite game has matching primal and dual values
nonclaims: the identity is for expected length and is not transferred to nonlinear queueing or peak objectives
the least-favorable prior is a game certificate rather than a claim about the true empirical source law

claims.title: Adversary timing phase change for shared robust codebooks
claims.scope: shared codebook mixtures under either an oblivious source-law adversary or a source-law adversary observing the realized codebook seed
assumptions: every selected deterministic codebook remains zero error
the seed-observing adversary may select a different TV-ball law for each realized codebook
the encoder chooses the codebook mixture before the seed is realized
nonclaims: a shared-randomness gain under an oblivious source law does not survive arbitrary correlation between the law and seed
the result does not decide which timing model is appropriate without a causal source model

claims.title: Exact Caratheodory support bounds for shared codebook and least-favorable prior mixtures
claims.scope: rational convex mixtures of deterministic state-length vectors in n dimensions and TV-ball prior vertices in the n minus one dimensional simplex
assumptions: only the convex barycenter affects the declared payoff
exact affine dependences are eliminated while preserving nonnegative weights and normalization
nonclaims: support size does not equal the Shannon entropy or exact random-bit cost of the shared seed
the bounds preserve barycenters and payoffs but need not preserve the original finite-game basic support

claims.title: Closed full-TV shared-randomness value for every complete confusion graph
claims.scope: the complete confusion graph K_n, full total-variation radius one, one-shot zero-error binary prefix coding, and an oblivious source law
assumptions: every source state requires a distinct message
the source law may be any finite distribution
a cyclic shared mixture may permute a near-balanced uniform-Huffman tree across states
nonclaims: the strict gain disappears when the state count is a power of two
the theorem concerns worst-law expected length and does not lower the hard zero-error message alphabet

claims.title: Full-TV three-state shared-randomness gain
claims.scope: the complete three-state confusion graph at total-variation radius one
assumptions: the source law is oblivious to the shared codebook seed
the three depth-one choices are mixed uniformly
nonclaims: the deterministic peak remains two bits
the gain is removed if the source law may condition on the realized seed

claims.title: Skew three-state shared-TV coding threshold at seven fifteenths
claims.scope: K3 with nominal prior (4/5,1/10,1/10) under shared-randomness TV-robust expected prefix coding
assumptions: the two low-probability states are symmetrized
the source law is selected from the TV ball independently of the realized seed
nonclaims: seven fifteenths is specific to the declared prior and three-tree code universe
the phase change is an optimization transition rather than a physical phase transition

claims.title: Bounded exact shared-TV vertex, game, replay, and sparsification audit
claims.scope: bounded finite rational TV balls, confusion graphs, complete prefix trees, finite games, and convex sparsifications checked by the repository
assumptions: all configured event-basis, partition, tree, candidate, dominance, game, and affine-elimination searches complete
vertex maxima are compared with independent mass transport
all labeled three-vertex graphs and closed complete-graph values through sixteen states are checked
nonclaims: bounded exact agreement is not a large-instance runtime guarantee
a cap failure is not an optimum, impossibility, statistical coverage, or empirical evidence certificate
